anomalies.observed: The anodes (pin 2) of D3 (LED_GREEN), D6 (LED_GREEN) and D7 (LED_YELLOW) are tied together into net /NET0053, but that net contains no other node: it is not connected to +3V3, +5V, or any driver. Their cathodes (pin 1) go through R71/R96/R68 to the CM4 open-collector LED outputs (Module2 pin 15 Ethernet_nLED3, pin 21 PI_nLED_Activity, pin 17 Ethernet_nLED2).
anomalies.expected: For an LED driven by an active-low open-collector output, the anode must be tied to a supply (here +3V3, the same rail the other indicator LEDs D1/D15/D20 use). The design intent is Ethernet link/activity and Pi activity indication, so these anodes should sit on the +3V3 net.

evidence.quote: breaking out GPIO, Ethernet, USB, camera connectors, and an RTC

anomalies.impact: The Ethernet link/activity LEDs and the Pi activity LED can never conduct (no anode supply and no load on the CM4 LED pins), so these status indicators are dead on the assembled board.

parsed.summary: The connectivity is largely consistent with the spec (16 MHz crystals on both MCP2515s, SM712 TVS on the CAN lines, LTC4412 ideal-diode path, etc.), but the anodes of D3/D6/D7 form an isolated net /NET0053 with no connection to any supply or driver, leaving the Ethernet/Pi activity LEDs unable to light.
